text:
marta: APAC GPU pool `pool-apac-2` is showing a correctable ECC spike across several hosts. 8 cards have >200 correctables in last 10m, Xid stream rising. I throttled new scheduling but didn't trigger autodrain. Anyone on call? :warning:

liam: looking now. which racks/hosts? any recent firmware push?

marta: host list from alert: `apac-n1-07`, `apac-n1-08`, `apac-n2-03` (partial). No firmware pushes in last 48h. networking flaps around 12:14 UTC but that seems unrelated.

oncall-bot: [ALERT] ecc_correctable_rate high on pool-apac-2 (8 cards). Alert ID: A-98721. See dashboard: https://grafana.company/internal/d/GPUs/pool-apac-2?orgId=1

kavi: quick thought: current auto-drain policy triggers at 250 correctables / 5m per card. That threshold works for noisy single-card failures but this looks correlated across a small subset. Auto-drain could starve the region if we evict too many at once.

liam: +1. we should gate auto-drain with an extra signal: either card-specific predictive SNR or cross-host correlation score. If 3+ cards across hosts in same rack spike together, prefer soft-degrade (reduce assignments) not full drain.

sam_g: can we do model-level fallback instead? route latency-sensitive traffic to dedicated pools in us-west for next 30m, and drop noncritical work to cheaper half-precision queue. Less churn than draining and cheaper than failover.

marta: good idea. capacity-wise we have ~12% spare in us-west reserved pools if we throttle batch sizes. But need ops consent for cross-region bursting.

liam: propose temporary playbook changes for correlated spikes: 1) if clustered spikes (>=3 hosts or >=5 cards in same rack) within 10m -> set pool to "graceful-degrade": apply per-host assignment cap 0.5x and disable new long sequences; 2) after degrade, run health-scan (nvml-check + self-test) and collect full `dmesg`/Xid logs; 3) only invoke autodrain if individual card exceeds 500 correctables in 5m or has persistent Xid slips (>=3 Xid per 10m) after graceful-degrade.

kavi: +1 but add cooldown: once we autodrain a card we should have a 2h re-evaluation window before permanent replacement to avoid replace-flapping during transient infra issues. Also add cost tag so replacements go through finance approval above $X.

marta: can we enrich telemetry first? right now the alert is just count-based. Need: per-card SNR, transient PCIe resets, host power events, and rack-level temp deltas. I can file a ticket to metrics for new labels.

ops-bot: created ticket MET-4839 to add `gpu_snr`, `pci_reset_count`, `rack_temp_delta` to ecc metric stream.

sam_g: for immediate mitigation, I'll open a regional routing rule to shift 20% of traffic off pool-apac-2 to us-east/dedicated pools, and set conservative batch windows. That should buy us 45-90m.

liam: while sam does that, i'll run this quick prom query to snapshot problem cards:```
max by (card,host) (increase(ecc_correctable_total[10m]))
```

marta: paste logs once you have them. If we see PCIe resets + correctables, escalate to hardware replacements. If only ECC correctables without resets, prefer firmware/kernel retries and avoid immediate swap.

kavi: also flag gradle-runbook change: add human-in-loop toggle for autodrain in APAC until we roll new SNR gating. If we are within maintenance window, allow automated drains; otherwise require two oncall approvals.

marta: decision for now: 1) apply graceful-degrade policy for pool-apac-2 (liam/kavi to push), 2) sam_g to shift 20% traffic and set batch caps, 3) ops-bot ticket created for telemetry, 4) hold autodrain unless card crosses 500/5m or persistent Xid after degrade. I'll coordinate postmortem if replacements occur.

liam: applying per-host cap now. logs incoming.

oncall-bot: Action taken: set pool `pool-apac-2` to mode=graceful-degrade by liam at 2026-03-18T12:20:05Z

sam_g: traffic shift done, batch cap lowered to 0.6x. monitoring for 30m. :thumbsup:

marta: thanks. will watch metrics and call hardware if we see resets. If anyone sees policy edge-cases (e.g., bursty eval jobs) ping me immediately.

kavi: I'll draft the short-term playbook blurb and add the two-approver gate for autodrain in APAC. will share in #eng-infra ops-docs later today.

liam: logs show 3 hosts with repeated Xid codes 83 and 31 plus temp spikes at rack PDU. Looks like a power rail glitch. I'll add note to MET ticket.

marta: perfect. closing loop: keep this thread for updates. I'll timestamp final status when resolved.

oncall-bot: [RESUME] alert A-98721 acknowledged and mitigated to degrade mode. Next check-in scheduled in 25m.
